name: application-range-dual-input
title: Range Dual Input
description: Paired min/max number fields for filtering by a numeric range, with a built-in error state when the minimum exceeds the maximum.
useWhen: Filtering a dataset by a numeric range such as price, quantity, or a date offset, where users type exact bounds.
A slider isn't precise enough and users need to enter exact numbers.
You want built-in validation that the minimum can't exceed the maximum.
avoidWhen: A visual drag interaction is more useful than typed precision — use a dual-thumb slider instead.
Only one bound matters (e.g. 'at least X') — a single number input is simpler than a pair.
The range is over dates rather than plain numbers — use date-range-picker instead.
responsiveBehavior: The pair of fields sits in a fixed max-w-xs row that fills its container's available width up to that cap at all breakpoints.
accessibility: Each field has a visually hidden label distinguishing minimum from maximum for screen reader users.
aria-invalid and aria-describedby are set on both fields together when the range is invalid, pointing at a single shared alert message.
The error message uses role="alert" so it's announced as soon as the invalid state appears.

variants.title: Range dual input
variants.description: Valid min/max price range with a dollar-sign prefix on each field.
accessibility: Both fields are reachable in a natural min-then-max tab order.

variants.title: Range dual input (Dark)
variants.description: Range dual input adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Field border and text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.

variants.title: Invalid range
variants.description: Error state when the minimum value is not less than the maximum, with both fields ringed red and a shared alert message.
accessibility: Both invalid fields share the same aria-describedby target so the single error message is announced once, not duplicated.

variants.title: Invalid range (Dark)
variants.description: Invalid range error state adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Error border and message colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
